analyst_view.overall: Early view: Frank Lampard's Coventry (17th, seven defeats in 10) host Unai Emery's Aston Villa (10th) in a revived local rivalry; Villa already won the League Cup meeting at this ground in September. Villa host PSG in the Champions League on Tuesday 8 December, so they have time to recover. Coventry's injuries before the international break (Haji Wright, Josh Eccles, Luke Woolfenden, Aurele Amenda) looked short-term and should have cleared by mid-December.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean higher: Coventry create chances but leak goals (5-0 at Brighton, 3-1 at Everton after leading), and Villa have conceded 11 in their recent run, including the 4-4 at Old Trafford after leading twice.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Neither side's recent games point to an unusual corner count, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, which looks low for a local rivalry with Coventry fighting relegation. Coventry press hard and Lampard has been frustrated with officials, so I expect more edge than usual.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, already a high figure. Both sides attack openly and defend loosely, which supports it, but I see no reason to go above it this far out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.1 shots on target. Coventry have been wasteful in front of goal, while Villa's attack, with Tammy Abraham scoring twice in the cup meeting, is sharper, so I stay with the number.
